title: Capstone: deal pitch to a mock committee
summary: Bring everything together in a one-page deal pitch and present it to a mock investment committee.
outcomes: Summarize a deal on one page.
Defend your valuation, financing and risks.

lessons.title: Writing the one-page pitch
lessons.body:
Lenders, partners and investors want to understand a deal quickly. A one-page pitch is the discipline of saying only what matters.

## The sections
1. **The business:** what it does, for whom, and why it lasts.
2. **Why you:** your edge, from your thesis.
3. **The numbers:** revenue, adjusted earnings, price, multiple.
4. **The capital stack:** sources of funds, debt service coverage and your take-home pay.
5. **Key risks and mitigations:** the top three from diligence and what you will do about each.
6. **The first 100 days:** three priorities.
7. **The ask:** what you want from the reader.

Use a real or practice deal from your earlier modules. Every number should trace back to one of your practical outputs.

lessons.title: Facing the mock committee
lessons.body:
In a search fund, the committee is your investors. For a self-funded buyer, it may be your lender, a partner or a mentor. Practise with people who will ask hard questions.

## Questions to expect
- "What happens if your largest customer leaves?"
- "Which add-backs are you least sure about?"
- "What if cash flow falls 20% in year one? Can you still pay the debt?"
- "Why is the seller selling now?"
- "What do you not know yet?"

## How to answer
Be direct. If you do not know, say so and say how you will find out. Committees trust buyers who name their own risks.

## After the session
Write down every question you could not answer well. Each one points to work you still need to do.

## Practical output
Submit your **one-page deal pitch**, present it to a mentor or peer group acting as the committee, and revise it once based on their feedback.

practicalOutput.title: One-page deal pitch
practicalOutput.description: A one-page summary of a deal, presented to a mock committee and revised once.
steps: Fill in all seven sections on one page.
Trace every number to a previous practical output.
Stress-test cash flow down 20% in the calculator.
Present to at least two people acting as a committee.
Revise once and record what changed.

quiz.question: What should every number in your pitch trace back to?
options: Your earlier practical outputs and evidence
quiz.explanation: Traceable numbers build trust with a committee.

quiz.question: How should you answer a question you cannot answer yet?
options: Say you do not know and how you will find out
quiz.explanation: Committees trust buyers who are honest about what they do not know.

quiz.question: Why stress-test cash flow down 20%?
options: To see whether you can still pay debt in a bad year
quiz.explanation: A downside test shows whether the structure survives a weak year.

quiz.question: Which section names what you want from the reader?
